title: Comparison: Lok Sabha vs Rajya Sabha

blocks.content: The Lok Sabha represents the people of India as a whole, while the Rajya Sabha represents the states and Union Territories of the Indian Union.

rows: Permanent Body (6-year term for members; 1/3rd retire every 2 years)
Exclusive power to introduce and pass
Limited role (14 days delay; cannot reject or amend)
Passes No-Confidence Motion against Council of Ministers
Exclusive powers under Article 249 (State List) and Article 312 (All-India Services)

items: Money Bills (Article 110) can only be introduced in Lok Sabha; Rajya Sabha has no power to amend or reject them and must return them within 14 days.
Article 249 empowers Rajya Sabha alone to authorize Parliament to make laws on matters listed in the State List in the national interest.
Article 312 grants Rajya Sabha the exclusive power to initiate the creation of one or more new All-India Services.
In a joint sitting of Parliament (Article 108) summoned to resolve a legislative deadlock, the Speaker of Lok Sabha presides.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Lok Sabha is the Lower House (House of the People), whose members are directly elected by citizens through universal adult suffrage.
Rajya Sabha is the Upper House (Council of States), whose members are indirectly elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies.
The Lok Sabha holds exclusive financial authority; Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and cannot be dissolved, with one-third of its members retiring every second year.
The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha, whereas the Vice President of India acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
